High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by order of framing charges dated 18-12-2020 passed by 10th Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior (MP) in Sessions Trial No. 214 of 2015, present revision under Section 397 r/w Section 401 of CrPC has been preferred by applicant- Bharat Kapoor whereby, charges under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC have been framed.

(2) Facts giving rise to present revision in short are that on 22-07- 2014, complainant Rajesh Jamdar lodged a computerized complainant with Police Station Huzrat Kotwali, Lashkar, Gwalior alleging therein that he had opened a current account number no.244628 of her unmarried sister Rajni Raje Jamdar at Bada Post Office because his sister was unmarried, used to be sick due to which, he had deposited Rs.15 lac in the said current account for expenses of his sister.

entities.text: Police Station Huzrat Kotwali, Lashkar, Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: His sister died on 01-03- 2014 and after receiving her death certificate from Municipal Corporation, Gwalior on 10-03-2014, he gave a written information about the death of his sister on 14-03-2014 to Postmaster Ramgopal Shakya and Assistant Postmaster Narendra Singh in connection with stopping the current account of his sister and took receipt of same.

After presenting receipt, he came to know that from said current account of his sister deceased Rajni Raje Jamdar, Postmaster Ram Gopal Shakya and Assistant Postmaster Narendra Singh and sub-ordinate postal staffs posted at window of the post-office, namely, Bharti Kaur, Vashu Shrivastava, Mrs. Sonali Agrawal, B.R.
Sindhe, Rahul Gupta and Sarla Bhagat and others, despite being known about the stoppage of account of his sister deceased on 14-03- 2014 by taking illegal benefits from Munna Shakya, Naresh Shakya, Kishori Shakya and Rajkumar Jatav and in connivance with dishonestly and cheating by forging signature of his sister deceased on the withdrawal form and after death of his sister deceased by obtaining passbook, PAN Card, AADHAR Card, Ration Card and other documents, conspired to withdraw Rs.7,35,000/- from the account of his sister deceased on different dates and distributed it among themselves.
All the accused persons conspired and cheated to extort the aforesaid money.
The criminal act of conspiracy with intent to cause loss by forgery and conspiracy to commit fraud has been committed.

For this reason, a complaint was filed against them on the basis of which Crime No. 37 of 2015 was registered for commission of offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471,
120-B, 34 of IPC at PS Huzrat Kotwali, Lashkar, Gwalior.

During investigation, on the basis of evidence of co-accused Kishori Shakya and Rajkumar Jatav recorded under Section 27 of Evidence Act, present applicant was made an accused in connection with aforesaid crime.
Charge sheet was submitted in the case against all the accused persons except the present applicant who was absconding and the investigation was continued against him under Section 173(8) of CrPC.
During investigation, applicant has been made an accused by police prima facie in connection with commission of aforesaid crime in connivance with other co-accused.
From his possession on 12-07-2015, handwriting of applicant, signature on the withdrawal form in six copies of which his signatures were annexed and six bank cheques were seized by police.

After going through materials and documents produced by police, the 10 th Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior in Sessions Trial No.214 of 2015 framed charges against present applicant for aforesaid offences under Sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of IPC.

Being dissatisfied with order of Bharat Kapoor vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156727981/
2 framing charges, present revision has been preferred at the instance of applicant.

sentences.text: (3) It is contended by learned Counsel for the applicant that the applicant is not named either in the complaint or in the impugned FIR.

As per rules of Post Office, the agent only brings investors in the savings account and other accounts and gets their accounts opened and apart from the above, the agent does not perform any other work.

The withdrawal form in the post-office has to be received and verified by Clerk concerned in relation to withdrawal of money from account holder and work of matching signature etc. would have been done by Clerk concerned and if concerned Clerk finds information on the withdrawal form is correct, then he/she puts signature of Officer of post office and then makes payment as per the rules.

Even according to prosecution story, no such allegation has been made against the applicant which appears that he has cheated either complainant or deceased and has prepared any forged documents with intention of cheating and with a view to earn any monetary benefits or profits.

It is further contended that as per story of prosecution, document on which signature of the applicant is said to be is not such a document on the basis of which it appears that any profit has been earned by the applicant and the documents bearing signature have been verified by the handwriting expert.

According to investigation conducted by police in relation to documents on which the forged documents have been prepared by applicant, the report of handwriting expert has been received to the effect that the signatures are not that of applicant but that are of either complainant or deceased.

It is further contended that according to prosecution story, other Postal Department employees including postmaster, assistant postmaster and other postal staffs have been told to be involved in crime and the pplicant has been involved in the case only on the basis of being an agent and on the basis of memorandum of Kishori Shakya and Rajkumar Jatav.
It is further contended that no money of any kind has been recovered from possession of the present applicant.
There is no such evidence available on record on the basis of which, the Court below has wrongly passed order of framing charges against the applicant.

Based on the report of the handwriting expert, it cannot be said that the present applicant had made any forgery or had he made any active role in gaining any benefits or earn any profits in connivance with other co- accused persons by fraudulently and dishonestly.
Prima facie, no offence is made out against the present applicant.

It is further contended that the Court is required to evaluate materials and documents available on record with a view to finding out if the fact emerging therefrom taken at their face value disclose the existence of all ingredients constituting alleged offences..
Thus, the applicant deserves to be discharged from the charges levelled against him.
(4) Per contra, the revision is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State.

It is contended that while exercising the power under revision, the charges are not liable to be quashed when the same is liable to be established by way of evidence before the trial and this Court is not required to evaluate the materials in the record and appreciate as charges are not made out and the applicant is entitled to the acquittal.

It is further contended that under Section 173 CrPC challan presented by police,
complaint/First Information Report, the evidence of witnesses and other documents were considered and arguments of parties were also considered before the Court below.
There is prima facie sufficient material available on record against him for framing of charges for aforesaid offences.

Hence, revision is liable to be dismissed as charges have been framed and, therefore,
legitimate prosecution may not be stifled in the midway.

sentences.text: (5) Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned order as well as the documents available on record.
(6) Before considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, this Court thinks it apposite to consider the scope of interference at the stage of framing of charges.

(7) The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan v. Fatehkaran Mehdu (2017) 3 SCC 198,
has observed as under:-
"26. ......................... the scope of interference under Section 397 CrPC at a stage,
when charge had been framed, is also well-settled.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan v. Fatehkaran Mehdu (2017) 3 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
At the stage of framing of a charge,
the Court is concerned not with the proof of the allegation rather it has to focus on the material and form an opinion whether there is strong suspicion that the accused has committed an offence, which if put to trial, could prove his guilt.
The framing of charge is not a stage, at which stage final test of guilt is to be applied.

Thus, to hold that at the stage of framing the charge, the Court should form an opinion that the accused is certainly guilty of committing an offence, is to hold something which is neither permissible nor is in consonance with the scheme of the Code of Criminal Procedure."
(8) In view of above law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court is having limited jurisdiction to interfere in the present matter.

At the time of framing of charges, the Court below or trial Court is only obligatory to examine whether on the basis of allegations in FIR/complaint and materials collected by the police during the investigation, prima facie charges are made out against the accused or not.
If ingredients of charges are there and on which, that the offence is said to have been made out or not, it is for prosecution to establish by way of evidence.
If ingredients of charges are there in the charge sheet, then the Court is bound to frame the charges under the Penal enactment.

On going through the impugned order and documents available on record, in the case at hand, it appears to be true that during the investigation the witnesses have stated that along with the postmaster, assistant postmaster and other postal staff including clerk, the applicant was also involved in misappropriation of amount to the tune of Rs.7, 35,000/- of the deceased (sister of complainant).

In such a situation, on the basis of materials and documents collected as well as produced by police, the learned trial Court has passed an order of framing charges against the applicant and did not commit any error or illegality in passing the order of framing charges.
Accordingly, revision being devoid of merits, is hereby dismissed.

(DEEPAK KUMAR AGARWAL) JUDGE MKB MAHENDRA BARIK 2023.06.20 14:23:24 +05'30'
